item.title: SPC Oct 11, 2026 1630 UTC Day 1 Convective Outlook
item.description:
SPC 1630Z Day 1 Outlook 
Day 1 Convective Outlook
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1129 AM CDT Sun Oct 11 2026

Valid 111630Z - 121200Z

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PARTS OF
NORTH CAROLINA AND VIRGINIA...

...SUMMARY...
A few tornadoes are possible across parts of North Carolina and
Virginia through the late afternoon.  Additional storms with
isolated severe gusts will be possible in parts of the Desert
Southwest and Four Corners region.

...NC/VA vicinity...
Midday water-vapor imagery shows a dry slot/vorticity lobe wrapping
through the base of the larger-scale remnants/cyclone associated
with Isaias and progressing eastward across the southern
Appalachians/Carolinas.  Surface analysis places a triple point over
northwest NC with a maritime warm frontal zone draped east-northeast
into the DelMarVa.  Despite considerable cloud cover according to
visible-satellite imagery, surface temperatures are gradually
warming into the mid to upper 70s across eastern NC and far
southeast VA.  This modest heating has led to the development of
around 1000 J/kg MLCAPE across eastern NC and weaker buoyancy
farther north near Richmond, VA (a few hundred J/kg).  The forced
band of broken thunderstorm activity moving east across NC will
likely be the primary feature for severe weather across this general
region through the late afternoon.  A few supercells embedded within
the north-south oriented band will potentially pose a risk for a few
additional tornadoes and perhaps an isolated risk for strong to
locally severe gusts (see MCD 2361 for short-term details).  Have
added a level-1 intensity highlight for the area of greatest
tornadic supercell potential through mid afternoon.  By late this
afternoon, it is possible (albeit uncertain) that a narrow corridor
adequately destabilizes ahead of triple point as it develops
northeastward into central VA.  If sufficient destabilization occurs
and sustained/robust storms also develop, a localized tornado/wind
threat could ensue prior to sunset.

...Desert Southwest/Eastern Great Basin...
Remnants of tropical cyclone Rachel are currently centered in the
CA/NV/AZ border vicinity, at the base of a broad upper trough
covering much of the western CONUS.  These remnants are forecast to
progress northeastward today, moving quickly through the Great Basin
and ending the period over central/eastern MT.  Persistent
large-scale forcing for ascent and the aforementioned moisture will
support scattered thunderstorms.  Strong low to mid-level
southwesterly flow will result in occasionally intense bowing
segments capable of strong gusts, particularly in any areas
that can experience filtered daytime heating.

..Smith/Barnes.. 10/11/2026

item.title: SPC Oct 11, 2026 1730 UTC Day 2 Convective Outlook
item.description:
SPC 1730Z Day 2 Outlook 
Day 2 Convective Outlook
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1203 PM CDT Sun Oct 11 2026

Valid 121200Z - 131200Z

...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

...SUMMARY...
No severe weather is expected Monday through Monday night.

...Upper Midwest/Great Lakes...

An upper shortwave trough will develop northeast from the central
High Plains to the Great Lakes on Monday. This will bring a belt of
mildly enhanced westerly mid/upper flow across the region, with an
increasing southwesterly low-level jet expected by Monday evening
from the Mid-MS Valley into MI. At the surface, low pressure will
shift east across MN/WI/MI, with a trailing cold front surging
east/southeast across the central Plains and Upper Midwest. A warm
front will be oriented west to east across northern WI to northern
Lower MI. Elevated thunderstorms may develop by 00z near and north
of this boundary on the edge of the increasing low-level jet and
stronger warm advection ahead of the surface low/cold front. Cooling
aloft will result in a plume of steep midlevel lapse rates
supporting modest elevated instability. Small hail may occur with
stronger updrafts within the modestly sheared environment across
northern WI/the U.P. of MI and portions of northern Lower MI during
the evening and overnight hours. Overall severe potential is
expected to remain limited by modest instability and capping across
the warm sector, precluding severe probabilities.

...Southwest/Great Basin...

Lingering moisture across the Southwest and Great Basin will support
scattered showers and thunderstorms within enhanced deep-layer
southwesterly flow ahead of an approaching upper low and attendant
trough. Meager destabilization will limit severe potential, though
some gusty winds are possible given stronger synoptic flow.

...Southern High Plains...

A few thunderstorms will be possible along a surface trough/dryline
across western TX/eastern NM as low-level moisture returns north and
west across the southern Plains. Modest vertical shear and weak
instability should limit severe potential, though some locally gusty
outflow winds are possible given steepened low-level lapse rates due
to daytime heating into the upper 80s/low 90s.

..Leitman.. 10/11/2026

item.title: SPC Oct 11, 2026 1930 UTC Day 3 Severe Thunderstorm Outlook
item.description:
SPC 1930Z Day 3 Outlook 
Day 3 Convective Outlook
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0209 PM CDT Sun Oct 11 2026

Valid 131200Z - 141200Z

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PARTS OF
THE CENTRAL AND SOUTHERN PLAINS...

...SUMMARY...
Widely scattered severe storms appear possible over portions of the
central and southern High Plains Tuesday afternoon into night. More
isolated severe weather may occur into the mid Mississippi Valley,
and in parts of the Lower Great Lakes.

...Central/Southern Plains to Mid-MS Valley...

Enhanced mid/upper southwesterly flow will reside across the region
on Tuesday in advance of an eastward-propagating upper low over the
Great Basin to central Rockies vicinity. At the surface, weak lee
low development is forecast across southeast CO/southwest KS, with
surface troughing extending southward across the southern High
Plains. Meanwhile, a surface front will extend from the High Plains
low east/northeast across northern KS toward northern IL during the
evening. Southerly low-level flow and a strengthening low-level jet
will support mid 60s to near 70 F dewpoints across the warm sector
from portions of western TX into OK/KS and the Mid-MS Valley. While
midlevel lapse rates are not forecast to be particularly strong,
rich boundary layer moisture will foster 1000-2000 J/kg MLCAPE.

Where stronger heating occurs in closer proximity to the surface
trough and triple point from northwest TX into central KS,
supercells will be possible amid vertically veering wind profiles.
Damaging winds and a tornado or two appear possible within this zone
of better instability and shear. Convection is likely to increase
along the breadth of the surface front into the Lower MO/Mid-MS
Valley as warm advection increases during the evening and overnight
hours. This convection may tend to be elevated within isentropic
ascent atop the surface front, further supported by
boundary-parallel wind profiles. Midlevel temperatures are forecast
to be cooler, and MUCAPE could approach 1000-1500 J/kg. Marginal
hail and gusty winds may accompany this activity into the nighttime
hours.

...Lower Great Lakes...

Showers and thunderstorms are likely to be ongoing Tuesday morning
ahead of an approaching midlevel shortwave impulse over the Great
Lakes. Deep-layer westerlies will increase through the day as this
disturbance approaches, resulting in a moderately to strongly
sheared environment. If sufficient heating can occur, surface
dewpoints near 60 F will aid in modest destabilization, resulting in
a conditionally favorable environment for localized strong wind
gusts and perhaps a tornado.

..Leitman.. 10/11/2026
